City approves overnight transit pilot

NORTH HARBOR, Aug. 8

The city council approved a six-month overnight transit pilot after a public hearing on Friday. Two bus routes will operate every forty minutes between the central station and the hospital district.

"The goal is to measure demand before making a permanent timetable change," transit director Lena Ortiz said.

The agency will publish ridership, missed-trip, and on-time performance data each month. Funding comes from an existing service reliability reserve, according to the adopted resolution.

Council members requested a formal review after the first ninety days. The pilot begins in September and does not change daytime service.
